# The `headr` Package <a href="https://github.com/Cassinic/headr/"><img src="../man/figure/logo.png" alt="headr logo" style="border:none" align="right" height="182.25"></a>

## Introduction


The `headr` is a very flexible toolbox to interact with other table or figure packages. This document is to provide you with an examples of how to use `headr` to add titles and footnotes to the ggplot figures. 

First, the filename including the file extension and the full path of the spreadsheet which is used to manage titles and foonotes information must be provided.\cr Here's an example of using `headr` along with `ggplot` to generate figure outputs:

```{r setup}
# Load the necessary libraries
library(headr)
library(ggplot2)
library(magrittr)
library(glue)
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
# (to use |> version 4.1.0 of R is required, for lower versions we recommend %>% from magrittr)
 
# Title and footnote spreadsheet path and filename
filename_with_path <- "C:/Users/u066227/Rproj/sample_titles.xls"

# Obtain header (title, subtitle, population) with one functional call
head_list <- select_row_header(filename = filename_with_path, tnumber = "Figure 1.1")

# Obtain footnotes and ref notes (including program name, run timestamp, data sources) with one functional call
foot_list <- select_row_footer(filename = filename_with_path, tnumber = "Figure 1.1")

fig <- ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy)) + 
  geom_point(aes(colour = class)) + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE) + 
  theme(legend.position = "right") +
    labs(
    title = {paste(head_list, sep = "\n", collapse = "\n ")},
    caption = {paste(foot_list, sep = "\t", collapse = "\n")}) +
      theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 11)) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")
  )

fig
```

## Examples

### Simple Examples


In these examples, we're creating a simple plot using the `mtcars` dataset and adding titles and footnotes to it.

### Additional Note:

As is the custom to print the program name, run time stamp and data source at the very bottom of the graph.
